pages.headline: Jordan, thank you.
pages.pull_quote: Your ability to earn is your biggest asset. This protects it.
paragraphs: Thank you for letting us shop your income protection. We quoted three of the strongest names in individual disability insurance: The Standard, Principal and MassMutual. Each one would replace about two-thirds of your $75,000 income if an illness or injury kept you from working.

We recommend The Standard. For $1,827.79 a year it pays $4,060 a month if you can't do your own occupation, and it covers mental health and substance-related disabilities with no time limit. It also adds a Family Care Benefit, a survivor benefit and the option to grow your benefit 4% a year for six years without new health questions.

Principal is a close second at $7.97 less a year for a $4,000 benefit. All three start paying after a 90-day waiting period and continue to age 65. Page 4 shows how to lower the cost or extend coverage to age 67. Call or email me when you're ready and we'll start your application.

why.title: Why The Standard
why.text: Nearly the same price as Principal with a $60 higher monthly benefit, unlimited coverage for mental health and substance-related disabilities, and a Family Care Benefit.

why.title: Why Principal
why.text: The lowest premium, no extra charge to pay monthly, true own-occupation coverage, and partial benefits starting at a 15% income loss.

why.title: Why MassMutual
why.text: The highest benefit and a mutual company that may pay dividends. It costs $557.16 more a year, and mental health claims are limited to 24 months.

why.title: 90 or 180 days?
why.text: With a 180-day wait you'd cover about six months from savings or sick pay before benefits start. It saves $274.29 a year with The Standard.

why.title: Age 65 or 67?
why.text: Paying to age 67 lines up with full Social Security retirement age. It adds $226.33 a year with The Standard.

why.title: Worth a look
why.text: If you have six months of savings, The Standard with a 180-day wait to age 67 costs $1,745.83, less than the 90-day plan to 65, with two more years of protection.

pages.headline: What these plans won't pay for.
pages.lede: Every disability policy has exclusions and limits. Here is what each carrier's quote lists, so there are no surprises at claim time.

common.title: Self-inflicted injury
common.text: A disability caused by an intentionally self-inflicted injury.

common.title: War
common.text: A disability from declared or undeclared war or an act of war.

common.title: Crime & riot
common.text: A disability from committing a felony, an illegal occupation, or taking part in a riot.

common.title: Incarceration
common.text: No benefits while jailed or detained for more than about a week.

common.title: Undisclosed health history
common.text: A pre-existing condition left off the application may not be paid. Answer every health question fully.

common.title: Conditions excluded by name
common.text: Underwriting can exclude a specific condition. Any exclusion will be listed on the offer before you accept.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.text: Normal pregnancy or childbirth is not paid for the first 90 days. Complications are covered.

items.title: Pre-existing conditions
items.text: Looks back 365 days before the policy starts. Covered if disclosed and not excluded.

items.title: Mental health
items.text: No time limit on mental-disorder or substance-related claims.

items.title: Working past 65
items.text: The renewal option pays total disability only, for up to 24 months.

items.title: Military service
items.text: No benefits for active military duty, including the Reserves or National Guard.

items.title: Living abroad
items.text: Live outside the U.S. or Canada more than 6 months a year and benefits stop after 12 months.

items.title: Loss of license
items.text: Losing a professional license is not, by itself, a disability.

items.title: Pre-existing conditions
items.text: Undisclosed conditions are not paid in the first 2 years.

items.title: Mental health
items.text: The quote does not state a limit. We will confirm the policy wording before you apply.

items.title: Mental health
items.text: Mental-disorder and substance-related claims are paid up to 24 months each, unless you are hospitalized.

items.title: Pre-existing conditions
items.text: Undisclosed conditions are not paid in the first 2 years.

items.title: Disability after 60
items.text: If disability starts at 61 or later, the benefit period gets shorter (48 months down to 24).

items.title: Military service
items.text: The policy can be suspended during more than 90 days of active duty.

sections.title: How disability insurance works
rows: The check you receive each month (generally income-tax free) while you're disabled, about two-thirds of your income.
How long you must be disabled before benefits start. A longer wait lowers the premium; your savings or sick pay cover the gap.
How long benefits can last for one disability. To age 65 or 67 protects you through your working years.
You're considered disabled if you can't do the main duties of your own occupation, even if you could work in a different one.
If you can work but earn less because of an illness or injury, the policy pays a share of the benefit based on the income you lost.
The carrier can't cancel the policy, change it or raise your premium before age 65 as long as you pay on time.
Losing your sight, speech, hearing or the use of two limbs pays the full benefit even if you keep working.
While you're receiving benefits, you don't pay premiums.
As your income grows, you can add coverage without new health questions, so your protection keeps up with your pay.

callout.title: Why this matters
callout.text: Most long-term disabilities are caused by illness, not accidents: back and joint problems, cancer, heart conditions and mental health conditions lead the list. Because you pay the premium yourself, benefits are generally received income-tax free; check with your tax advisor.

info.title: About The Standard's eApply discount
info.text: The Standard's price includes a $96.20 discount for applying electronically with its online medical questionnaire. We'll apply that way so you keep the discount.

info.title: What underwriting looks like
info.text: Expect a health questionnaire, possibly a quick paramedical visit or lab sample, and proof of your income such as a recent tax return or pay stubs. We'll walk you through each step.
